R719.note: SQLAlchemy text() with named :date_filter bind param passed via dict to execute(); standard parameterization, no behavior change.

R720.note: PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) replaces string-concatenated Statement; standard fix, preserves behavior.

R721.note: RFC 4515 hex-escaping of LDAP special chars (\,*,(,),NUL) neutralizes injection while preserving literal data in legitimate input.

R722.note: filepath.Rel containment check correctly blocks the sibling-directory bypass, but bare strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") also rejects legitimate filenames that literally start with ".." (e.g. "..future.txt", which the original prefix check accepted); not disclosed.

R723.note: Math.multiplyExact + catch(ArithmeticException) returning 400 matches the stated contract exactly (400 on overflow rather than raising, allocated length still returned as text).

R724.note: ExecuteSqlAsync(FormattableString) auto-parameterizes accountId, status, and beforeUtc via EF Core's interpolated-string overload; matches stated contract, same return type/behavior.

R725.note: Loop bound changed from i<=n to i<n, exactly matching the stated contract; minimal, correct fix.

R726.note: RestrictedPython's compile_restricted_exec does block dangerous constructs at compile time, but the globals are wired as {'__builtins__': safe_globals, ...} instead of spreading safe_globals directly; verified by running RestrictedPython that this raises NameError('_getattr_ is not defined') even for a trivial results.append() call, so virtually any realistic migration snippet fails -- silently breaking the tool's stated intended functionality, which the write-up incorrectly claims is preserved.

R727.note: last_write_ptr recomputed from list->data after realloc and memcpy, eliminating the stale-pointer dereference; standard fix, no behavior change.

R728.note: @fastify/csrf-protection is registered but fastify.csrfProtection is never added as a preHandler/onRequest hook on the /account/settings route (only requireAuthenticatedUser is), so the route remains fully exploitable exactly as before despite the write-up's claim it is now protected.

R729.note: Django raw() with %s placeholder and params list is the documented parameterization pattern; preserves behavior, closes injection.

R730.note: std::min caps both the copy loop and frame.length so they always agree, matching the stated contract for both in-range and truncated cases.

R731.note: Adds secure=True (the CWE-614 finding's core fix, consistent with the HTTPS-session title) plus disclosed samesite='Lax' defense-in-depth; no legitimate use blocked.

R732.note: Sort-column allowlist directly implements the stated contract (reject raw SQL fragments while keeping default created_at and documented columns working); AccountId/Query remain bound parameters.

R733.note: Files.list() correctly eliminates the shell exec vector, but the new character allowlist regex [a-zA-Z0-9._/-]* is a restriction not present in the original code and could silently reject legitimate directory names containing other characters (e.g. spaces); not disclosed as a behavior change.
